title: Elena Verna on PLG, B2B Growth Loops, and Freemium Conversion
content:
Lenny Rachitsky: Welcome to Lenny's Podcast. Today my guest is Elena Verna, growth advisor and former Head of Growth at Amplitude, Miro, and SurveyMonkey. Elena, welcome to the show.

Elena Verna: Thanks for having me, Lenny. I'm excited to dive into product-led growth.

Lenny Rachitsky: Let's start with product-led growth. What is the single biggest misconception PMs have about PLG?

Elena Verna: The biggest misconception is thinking PLG is just self-serve signups or a free trial button on your website. True PLG is an organizational alignment where the product itself drives user acquisition, retention, and monetization. It is not a feature or a top-of-funnel hack; it is your core distribution loop.

Lenny Rachitsky: How should B2B companies choose between a freemium model and a free trial?

Elena Verna: Freemium works when your product has a high network effect or long time-to-value, giving users persistent value until they hit a clear usage boundary or feature wall. Free trials work best when the value proposition is immediate and high-touch, but users must evaluate full enterprise capabilities within 14 to 30 days. If your time-to-value exceeds 14 days, a free trial will kill your conversion rates because users drop off before experiencing the core aha moment.

Lenny Rachitsky: What about product-led sales or PLS? How does PLS layer on top of PLG?

Elena Verna: Product-led sales does not replace PLG; it harvest PLG usage. Instead of cold outbound calling, sales reps reach out to accounts that already exhibit active product usage signals—such as team invite velocity, feature adoption thresholds, or domain consolidation. Sales reps become consultants helping active user groups expand into enterprise contracts.
